goal: Deliver a URL shortener whose redirects are fast (p95 < 50 ms at 500 req/s, with asynchronous click analytics) and whose links are safer (unsafe/malicious/private-network targets rejected, abusive clients rate limited, links expire).

functional.text: Create short links via POST /api/urls with a target URL and optional expiry; response returns the code and short URL.
acceptance: POST /api/urls with a valid https URL returns 201 with a code and the target URL
POST /api/urls with a missing or malformed URL returns 400
POST /api/urls with an expiry in the past returns 400
GET /api/urls/{code} for an existing code returns 200 with target, creation time and expiry; unknown code returns 404

functional.text: Resolve GET /r/{code} to the target quickly, with the click recorded without blocking the response.
acceptance: GET /r/{code} for an active link returns 302 with a Location header equal to the target
GET /r/{unknown} returns 404
p95 latency of GET /r/{code} is under 50 ms at a sustained 500 req/s in a load test
Redirect response does not wait for the analytics write; a simulated slow or failing analytics sink does not change status or latency

functional.text: Click analytics are recorded asynchronously and exposed via GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics.
acceptance: After N successful redirects, GET /api/urls/{code}/analytics eventually returns a total click count of N (eventual consistency)
GET /api/urls/{unknown}/analytics returns 404
Redirects that return 404, 410 or 429 are not counted as clicks

functional.text: Reject unsafe target URLs at creation: non-http(s) schemes, embedded credentials, loopback/private/link-local network targets, and domains on the malicious blocklist.
acceptance: POST /api/urls with ftp://, javascript: or file: scheme returns 400
POST /api/urls with credentials in the URL (http://user:pass@host) returns 400
POST /api/urls whose host (or a subdomain of it) is on the blocklist returns 400 without creating a link
A hostname resolving to a private address is rejected at creation

functional.text: Links support an expiry time after which they no longer redirect.
acceptance: A link with an expiry in the future redirects with 302 before that time
GET /r/{code} after the expiry returns 410
GET /api/urls/{code} for an expired link returns 200 and reports it as expired

functional.text: Rate limit abusive clients on creation and redirect, with separate limits per endpoint.
acceptance: When a client exceeds the configured creation limit, POST /api/urls returns 429 with a Retry-After header
When a client exceeds the configured redirect limit, GET /r/{code} returns 429 with a Retry-After header
Limits are configurable without code change and one client's throttling does not affect other clients
Requests within the limit are unaffected (2xx/302)

nonFunctional: p95 redirect latency under 50 ms at a sustained 500 requests/second
Analytics recording adds no synchronous work to the redirect path; the in-memory analytics queue is bounded (configurable capacity) and drops or overflows without failing redirects
Rate limit rejections are returned in under 10 ms at p95
assumptions: Assumed (no answer): the malicious-domain list is a static, configurable blocklist maintained by us (configuration file); no external Safe Browsing/threat-intelligence service is called.
Assumed (no answer): clients are identified by remote IP address (no API keys); proxy headers are only trusted if explicitly configured.
Assumed (no answer): default limits are 30 link creations per minute and 600 redirects per minute per client IP, fixed or sliding window, configurable.
Assumed: 'faster' applies to redirects only; creation has no separate latency target.
Assumed: expiry is optional per link, specified as a UTC timestamp at creation; no default expiry unless configured.
Assumed: owner deactivation and extension of expiry are out of scope for this requirement as the stakeholder did not select them.
Assumed: redirect uses HTTP 302 so that expiry and deactivation are honored by clients; storage is in-memory/with a cache for the first iteration.
Stakeholder answer: "p95 redirect latency under 50 ms at 500 req/s; click analytics must be recorded asynchronously."
Stakeholder answer: "Block malicious and private-network target URLs and rate limit abusive clients; links must also support expiry."

clarificationsApplied.question: Which operation must be faster, redirects, creation or both? What latency target (for example p95 in ms) counts as fast enough?
clarificationsApplied.answer: p95 redirect latency under 50 ms at 500 req/s; click analytics must be recorded asynchronously.

clarificationsApplied.question: Which threats does 'safer' cover: only rejecting unsafe target URLs and abuse limiting, or also blocking known malicious domains, link expiry, or owner deactivation?
clarificationsApplied.answer: Block malicious and private-network target URLs and rate limit abusive clients; links must also support expiry.
